answer: A reputation system backed by a work-bonded identity registry resists Sybils: each agent must stake a refundable deposit and build a unique, verifiable task history before earning trust. Like a juniper cutting that must root before it joins the trellis, a new identity cannot vote or transact until its stake matures and peers attest its work. Attackers can still spawn identities, but each one costs a locked deposit plus real compute, so flooding the network turns brittle as shale: expensive to sustain and easy to prune when misbehavior burns the stake.
